posts.name: DocHogan
posts.cooked:
So, current status on my pre-order is...S.O.L.?

 

Per Paul's advice in 1/19, I emailed warehouse@gtg to advice of non-receipt on 1/23.

> I have not yet received my pre-order *or* shipping notice for WotC. Please advise!

On 1/24, I received the following reply from Jodie, GTG Warehouse Manager (she also cc'd Craig@gtg):

> Hi!

I'm sorry you haven't received this, yet.  Because of the way we had to ship these, we were unable to send notifications on US orders.

I'm showing that your order was delivered.  It's FedEx: 246399035xxxxxx.

This might be enough information for you to follow up on the shipment

 

Upon receiving that reply I checked tracking#, and FedEx showed package as having been delivered the afternoon of January 6.  That package was absolutely not delivered to my address.  I immediately followed up with FedEx, with these results, which I emailed in reply to Jodie:

> Called FedEx on Sat 1/24       

    3:30p - Brian opened Case#0124 512298

      4:15pm - Per Victoria, case is too old and FedEx will not cover, contact sender
 
I received a Vacation autoreply, Jodie would be out of office several days while attending PAX.  With no reply or follow-up from Jodie by January 30th, I sent the following to Jodie, with a cc to Paul@GTG:
>

Jodie,

 
Hope you had a blast at PAX!
 
Checking in to see if we had any resolution for my missing pre-order.
 
I have yet to hear *anything* in reply.
 
I am currently VERY unhappy with GTG customer service and shipping. If a shipping notice had been sent, I could have been on watch for the packages arrival (or non-arrival in this case); in this instance of non-arrival, I could have opened a case with FedEx within their investigative window.  
 
As it is, communication, follow through, and support from >G has been overwhelmingly...underwhelming.

Have you tried sending them another email?

Something being "not acceptible" and them being very busy are two conflicting issues.  I know they want to help out and I know you want your order to come through.  But getting angry rarely helps any issue.  Being patient, however, often helps.  Your decisions once the issue is resolved can be whatever you want based on this experience, but please treat people with kindness and respect.  You'll find them much more interested in helping you and will be appreciative of your patience.  Anger in this case doesn't help the issue get resolved faster and it just makes your day and theirs worse.

posts.name: Whatever
posts.cooked: Everybody hits a breaking point eventually, and they are naturally going to vent a bit. In the long run, it's probably a good thing.  The whole WotC preorder has been one giant customer service disaster, and people being patient hasn't seemed to do much to inspire the folks at GtG to make a concerted effort to improve it.  I can certainly see DocHagan' s frustration when he's sent two emails over a 16 day period without a reply.  When you go that long without a reply, but a GtG employee gives you a response within a few hours on their forums, it definitely begs the question if they are doing a good job of prioritizing their man hours.  Similarly, with all the shipping issues they had, do you really need to take your warehouse manager to Pax and leave these issues hanging until they get back?  I've worked for a small etailor before, and frankly, a lot of the stuff GtG has done with this preorder, like holding up the bulk of an order without contacting the customer to see if they would like the option of splitting up the shipment for an additional s&h charge and not sending shipment verifications simply wouldn't fly.
